prompt: List every category of the parent category Accessories with the names of its products. Keep a category that has no products: product_name is missing for it. Return two columns, in this order: category_name and product_name. Return one row for each product, plus one row for each Accessories category with no products. Any row order is fine.

output_contract.grain: one row per product, plus one per category with no products

hints: Next, join the products so that every Accessories category stays, even one with no products.
An inner join keeps only the categories that have products. The join type you need keeps every row of the table written first; the parent test is about categories, so WHERE is fine for it.
faded_shape:
SELECT c.category_name, p.product_name
FROM categories c
why_this_works: LEFT JOIN keeps every category; where no product matches, the product columns come back missing, and WHERE then keeps the Accessories categories.
